rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offer names one of two daughters without specifying which; at the marriage itself the bride becomes definite.
rows.anchor: فلا شبهة في أن هذا اللفظ ، وإن كان على الترديد لكنه عند التزويج عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contract was concluded for the shorter term of eight years, making the extra two years a voluntary gift.
rows.anchor: ولا شبهة في أن العقد وقع على أقل الأجلين ، فكانت الزيادة كالتبرع

rows.speaker: الفقهاء
rows.claim: Jurists may cite the passage to show that labor can serve as a marriage dower just as money can.
rows.anchor: والفقهاء ربما استدلوا به على أن العمل قد يكون مهرا كالمال

rows.speaker: الفقهاء
rows.claim: Jurists may also cite it for the permissibility of adding an increase to the agreed consideration.
rows.anchor: وعلى أن إلحاق الزيادة بالثمن والمثمن جائز ، ولكنه شرع من قبلنا فلا يلزمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These inferences concern a prior religious law and therefore do not bind Muslims as rulings.
rows.anchor: ولكنه شرع من قبلنا فلا يلزمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That earlier law permitted a guardian to stipulate a benefit for himself in the marriage arrangement.
rows.anchor: ويدل على أنه قد كان جائزا في تلك الشريعة أن يشرط للولي منفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That earlier law allowed marriage without a separate consideration owed to the woman.
rows.anchor: وعلى أنه كان جائزا في تلك الشريعة نكاح المرأة بغير بدل تستحقه المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That earlier law did not invalidate a marriage contract merely because it contained conditions not required by the contract itself.
rows.anchor: وعلى أن عقد النكاح لا تفسده الشروط التي لا يوجبها العقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾjurnī can mean that Moses works as the speaker’s hired laborer; alternatively, the verb can mean granting or assigning something to someone.
rows.anchor: تأجرني من أجرته إذا كنت له أجيرا وثماني حجج ظرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses the eight years as the object and understands the service as tending for eight years.
rows.anchor: وثماني حجج مفعول به ومعناه رعية ثماني حجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that the speaker will not impose the more complete of the two terms; a grave demand seems to divide one’s judgment between ability and inability.
rows.anchor: لا أريد أن أشق عليك بإلزام أثم الرجلين ، فإن قيل ما حقيقة قولهم شققت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he promises lenience in the herding work and will not demand extreme care in how Moses tends the flock.
rows.anchor: لا أريد أن أشق عليك في الرعي ولكني أساهلك فيها وأسامحك بقدر الإمكان

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The cited report calls the Prophet an excellent partner who did not act evasively, dishonestly, or quarrelsomely; al-Razi uses it to exemplify gentleness in dealings.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شريكي فكان خير شريك لا يداري ولا يشاري ولا يماري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised righteousness may mean good dealings and a gentle manner, or righteousness generally, which includes good dealings.
rows.anchor: الأول : يريد بالصلاح حسن المعاملة ولين الجانب والثاني : يريد الصلاح على العموم ويدخل تحته حسن المعاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker qualifies his promise with God willing because he depends on God’s enabling and assistance.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال إن شاء الله للاتكال على توفيقه ومعونته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked how the marriage contract can stand with this condition, given that saying “my wife is divorced if God wills” does not effect divorce, al-Razi answers that rulings differ between religious laws.
rows.anchor: هذا مما يختلف بالشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the third answer to the opponents’ claim that they abandoned religion to avoid losing worldly life: what God has is better and more lasting.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن هذا هو الجواب الثالث : عن تلك الشبهة لأن حاصل شبهتهم أن قالوا تركنا الدين لئلا تفوتنا الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better because its benefits are greater and free of the harms mixed into worldly benefits, where harms predominate.
rows.anchor: أما أنه خير فلوجهين أحدهما : أن المنافع هناك أعظم وثانيهما : أنها خالصة عن الشوائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife lasts because it is permanent, whereas worldly benefits end; compared with the infinite, the finite is as nothing, and each person’s worldly share is tiny beside the whole.
rows.anchor: أما أنها أبقى فلأنها دائمة غير منقطعة ومنافع الدنيا منقطعة ومتى قوبل المتناهي بغير المتناهي كان عدما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing worldly benefits over the greater afterlife benefits is a grave failure of reason; al-Shafi‘i says a bequest to the most intelligent should go to those devoted to obedience, who give little and gain much.
rows.anchor: ورحم الله الشافعي حيث قال : من أوصى بثلث ماله لأعقل الناس صرف ذلك الثلث إلى المشتغلين بطاعة الله

words: أَفَمَن وَعَدْنَٰهُ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا فَهُوَ لَٰقِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if worldly blessings ended without punishment, reason would still prefer the afterlife; the case is stronger when worldly life is followed by lasting punishment.
rows.anchor: لو قدرنا أن نعم الله كانت تنتهي إلى الانقطاع والفناء وما كانت تتصل بالعذاب الدائم لكان صريح العقل يقتضي ترجيح نعم الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison is phrased as a question to make acknowledgment of the afterlife’s superiority more forceful.
rows.anchor: وأورد هذا الكلام على لفظ الاستفهام ليكون أبلغ في الاعتراف بالترجيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muḥḍarīn here means those brought forward for punishment; the Qur’anic usage and the word’s sense of compelled attendance suit harm and distress, not pleasure.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص لفظ المحضرين بالذين أحضروا للعذاب أمر عرف من القرآن

none: The segment contains only the quoted verses.
The segment contains only the quoted verses.

words: وَمَا كُنتَ تَتْلُوا۟ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مِن كِتَٰبٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a further step in the argument: after the earlier analogy, al-Razi identifies the shared basis as the miracle proving that earlier books were revealed and that this Qur’an is revelation.
rows.anchor: ذكر أولا التمثيل بقوله : { وكذلك أنزلنا إليك } ( العنكبوت : 47 ) ثم ذكر الجامع وهو المعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That the Qur’an came through someone who neither wrote nor read is itself a miracle and establishes its revealed origin.
rows.anchor: ما علم كون تلك الكتب منزلة إلا بالمعجزة ، وهذا القرآن ممن لم يكتب ولم يقرأ عين المعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a literate Prophet could not have authored this inimitable discourse, but literacy would give opponents some ground for doubt; his actual condition leaves them no ground.
rows.anchor: فإن جميع كتبة الأرض وقرائها لا يقدرون عليه ، لكن على ذلك التقدير يكون للمبطل وجه ارتياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi reads “from someone like him” in the challenge as meaning someone like Muhammad, connecting the challenge to the Prophet’s inability to read or write.
rows.anchor: أي من مثل محمد عليه السلام وكقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also invokes the opening declaration that the Book has no doubt.
rows.anchor: وكقوله : { الم * ذالك الكتاب لا ريب فيه } ( البقرة : 1 / 2 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its presence in the hearts of the learned shows it is not human invention: an inventor says a work comes from his own thought, while someone memorizing another’s words says they are in his heart.
rows.anchor: من يكون له كلام مخترع يقول هذا من قلبي وخاطري ، وإذا حفظه من غيره يقول إنه في قلبي وصدري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Qur’an’s appearance in these believers’ hearts is not from any individual among them, and the ignorant cannot produce it, its source is God.
rows.anchor: لا يكون من صدر أحد منهم ، والجاهل يستحيل منه ذلك ظهور له من الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the proof, “disbelievers” was the stronger deterrent; after it, “wrongdoers” is stronger because denial now entails joining the polytheists in reality, with wrongdoers here meaning polytheists.
rows.anchor: قبل بيان المعجزة قيل لهم إن لكم المزايا فلا تبطلوها بإنكار محمد فتكونوا كافرين ، فلفظ الكافر هناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people acknowledge God as creator and provider yet leave worship for worldly adornment, al-Razi says God shows that what attracts them is nothing.
rows.anchor: لما بين أنهم يعترفون بكون الله هو الخالق وكونه هو الرزاق وهم يتركون عبادته ولا يتركونها إلا لزينة الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One distinction is that play means turning toward falsehood for fleeting pleasure, while lahw means turning away from truth; worldly life involves both.
rows.anchor: فالإقبال على الباطل لعب والإعراض عن الحق لهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, play is putting one activity first and intending to do the other later, while lahw is becoming absorbed in one and turning wholly from the other.
rows.anchor: فالأول لعب والثاني لهو ، والدليل عليه هو أن الشطرنج والحمام وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Chess and pigeon keeping are not conventionally called instruments of lahw, but stringed instruments are because their immediate pleasure distracts a person from everything else.
rows.anchor: والعود وغيره من الأوتار تسمى آلات الملاهي لأنها تلهي الإنسان عن غيرها لما فيها من اللذة الحالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For some people worldly life is play: they engage in it expecting to turn to worship and the afterlife later; for others it is lahw, and they forget the afterlife entirely.
rows.anchor: فالدنيا للبعض لعب يشتغل به ويقول بعد هذا الشغل أشتغل بالعبادة والآخرة ، وللبعض لهو يشتغل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative “this” fits the present context because it has just mentioned worldly life through the earth revived by rain; in the cited regret passage, the preceding scene is the afterlife, so it says simply “worldly life.”
rows.anchor: لأن المذكور من قبل ههنا أمر الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order reverses “play and lahw” in the regret passage: there, absorption in worldly life is remote; here, worldly life’s attraction makes absorption more likely, so lahw comes first.
rows.anchor: فنقول لما كان المذكور هناك من قبل الآخرة وإظهارهم للحسرة ، ففي ذلك الوقت يبعد الاستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regret passage only needs to say the afterlife is better, but people absorbed in worldly life need the stronger warning that real life is only in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ههنا الحال حال الاشتغال بالدنيا احتاج إلى رادع قوي فقال لا حياة إلا حياة الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi omits “for those who fear God” here because only the God-fearing find the afterlife better, whereas its lasting, eternal life is not restricted to one group.
rows.anchor: لأن الآخرة خير للمتقي فحسب أي المتقي عن الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥayawān is a verbal noun from ḥayya, like ḥayāh, but carries greater emphasis; the afterlife is the second and truly substantial life.
rows.anchor: الحيوان مصدر حي كالحياة لكن فيها مبالغة ليست في الحياة والمراد بالدار الآخرة هي الحياة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the afterlife earns this name because it contains increase and growth and is where full, true perception occurs.
rows.anchor: لما كانت الآخرة فيها الزيادة والنمو كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse exhorts people: they are attracted to giving one unit expecting two, but that gift does not grow with God, whereas zakat grows with Him, so they should give zakat more readily.
rows.anchor: ذكر هذا تحريضا يعني أنكم إذا طلب منكم واحد باثنين ترغبون فيه وتؤتونه وذلك لا يربوا عند الله والزكاة تنمو عند الله

rows.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that charity is placed in the Merciful’s hand and grows until it is like a mountain.
rows.anchor: كما أخبر النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( إن الصدقة تقع في يد الرحمن فتربوا حتى تصير مثل الجبل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The multiplied reward is at least tenfold; the multiplication concerns the good and reward of the act, not a literal tenfold quantity of the object given.
rows.anchor: وأقل ذلك عشرة أضعاف كل مثل لما آتى في كونه حسنة لا في المقدار فلا يفهم أن من أعطى رغيفا يعطيه الله عشرة أرغفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single loaf can earn a heavenly palace through mercy and ten like it through grace; the difference reflects generosity beyond the action’s ordinary worth.
rows.anchor: فبالرغيف الواحد يكون له قصر في الجنة فيه من كل شيء ثوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A king who ordinarily rewards a one-dirham gift with a thousand shows generosity by giving ten thousand; this illustrates divine multiplication beyond ordinary compensation.
rows.anchor: مثاله في الشاهد ، ملك عظيم قبل من عبده هدية قيمتها درهم لو عوضه بعشرة دراهم لا يكون كرما

none: The segment contains only the quoted verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura’s theme is disciplining the Prophet: it first treats his duty toward God and his family, then commands believers as God commands His messengers, beginning with reverence for Him.
rows.anchor: وجه تعلق الآية بما قبلها هو أن السورة أصلها ومبناها على تأديب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers may forget God, so they are commanded to remember Him continually; the Prophet does not forget, but is commanded to fear God because closeness can lessen fear and even the elect remain at risk.
rows.anchor: المؤمن قد ينسى ذكر الله فأمر بدوام الذكر ، أما النبي لكونه من المقربين لا ينسى ولكن قد يغتر المقرب من الملك بقربه منه فيقل خوفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description “much” is apt because, as al-Razi has explained elsewhere, there is no impediment to remembering God.
rows.anchor: قد ذكرنا أن الله في كثير من المواضع لما ذكر وصفه بالكثرة إذ لا مانع من الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From Us” highlights David’s special rank: although God’s favors are general, prophecy is a particular gift bestowed on some.
rows.anchor: فكذلك إيتاء الله الفضل عام لكن النبوة من عنده خاص بالبعض

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses the call to the mountains as an apposition to “favor,” so the favor means God’s saying, “O mountains, echo with him.”
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري : { من جبال } بدل من قوله : { فضلا }

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows “O mountains” to be an apposition to “We gave,” meaning, “We said: O mountains.”
rows.anchor: أو من آتينا ومعناه قلنا يا جبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read with a doubled wāw from taʾwīb, or with a quiescent wāw and ḍamma on the hamza from awb; the former means repeated echoing, the latter return, and another gloss is traveling with him.
rows.anchor: قرىء أوبي بتشديد الواو من التأويب وبسكونها وضم الهمزة أوبي من الأوب وهو الرجوع والتأويب الترجيع ، وقيل بأن معناه سيرى معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “they glorify” is explained as coming from sabāḥah, a particular kind of movement.
rows.anchor: قالوا : هو من السباحة وهي الحركة المخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭayr is read in the accusative, coordinated with the grammatical position of the vocative, or in the nominative, coordinated with its surface form.
rows.anchor: قرىء { والطير } بالنصب حملا على محل المنادى والطير بالرفع حملا على لفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains and birds are singled out because rocks seem immovable and birds seem prone to flee, making their agreement striking; if they comply, other things should do so more readily.
rows.anchor: ذكر الجبال ، لأن الصخور للجمود والطير للنفور تستبعد منهما الموافقة ، فإذا وافقه هذه الأشياء فغيرها أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some people nevertheless did not respond to David; their hearts were hardened even more than stones.
rows.anchor: ثم إن من الناس من لم يوافقه وهم القاسية قلوبهم التي هي أشد قسوة من الحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We softened iron” can coordinate with the implied “We said” in the mountain address or with “We gave him favor.”
rows.anchor: والمعطوف عليه يحتمل أن يكون قلنا المقدر في قوله يا جبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made iron as soft as wax in David’s hand; since fire can soften and melt it, this is no cause to doubt God’s power.
rows.anchor: ألان الله له الحديد حتى كان في يده كالشمع وهو في قدرة الله يسير ، فإنه يلين بالنار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says David asked God to make him independent of public funds, so God softened iron and taught him to make armor.
rows.anchor: قيل / إنه طلب من الله أن يغنيه عن أكل مال بيت المال فألان له الحديد وعلمه صنعة اللبوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose armor because it protects the God-given soul and helps preserve honored human life; thus an armorer is better than an archer or swordsman.
rows.anchor: لأنه وقاية للروح التي هي من أمره وسعى في حفظ الآدمي المكرم عند الله من القتل

none: The segment contains only the quoted verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After clear proofs, the point invites reflection: a lying Prophet would fear his own sin, which no one else can bear, and God does not need human worship; if people stray, no one carries their burden.
rows.anchor: لما بين الحق بالدلائل الظاهرة والبراهين الباهرة ذكر ما يدعوهم إلى النظر فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul bears another’s sin, unlike the claim that others can say, “Follow our path and we will carry your sins.”
rows.anchor: وليس كما يقول : { ءامنوا اتبعوا سبيلنا ولنحمل خطاياكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A burden-bearing one” means a soul bearing sin; omitting an explicit noun is clear because the descriptive quality is inseparable from its subject.
rows.anchor: أي نفس وازرة ولم يقل ولا تزر نفس وزر أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “no burden-bearing one” makes clear that each soul bears its own burden but not another’s; simply saying “no soul bears another’s burden” could also include someone who bears no burden at all.
rows.anchor: بين أنها تزر وزرها ولا تزر وزر الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording denies help both unsolicited and after a request: a needy person may endure quietly until the burden becomes so great that they ask.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن أحدا لا يحمل عن أحد شيئا مبتدئا ولا بعد السؤال ، فإن المحتاج قد يصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the soul heavily burdened rules out lack of compassion as the reason no one helps: the load is severe, yet none of it is carried by another.
rows.anchor: يعني ليس عدم الوزر لعدم كونه محلا للرحمة بالثقل بل لكون النفس مثقلة ولا يحمل منها شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a close relative will not carry the burden: the sinner may be able to bear it, the other is heavily burdened, the request invites mercy, and kinship invites help, yet each remains under their own load.
rows.anchor: أي يحصل جميع المعاني الداعية إلى الحمل من كون النفس وازرة قوية تحتمل وكون الأخرى مثقلة

words: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَأَقَامُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet has already brought all possible guidance; warning benefits only those whose hearts are filled with awe and whose outward lives show worship.
rows.anchor: فلا تنذر إنذارا مفيدا إلا الذين تمتلىء قلوبهم خشية وتتحلى ظواهرهم بالعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of God describes the inward act, while establishing prayer describes outward action, parallel to the pairing of faith with righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: في ذلك المعنى ، ثم لما بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After stating that no one bears another’s burden, the passage adds that purification benefits the person who purifies themself.
rows.anchor: بين أن الحسنة تنفع المحسنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If purification’s benefit or sin’s consequence is not visible in this life, both will become apparent in the afterlife when all return to God.
rows.anchor: إن لم تظهر فائدته عاجلا فالمصير إلى الله يظهر عنده في يوم اللقاء في دار البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After contrasting guidance and misguidance, al-Razi identifies the believer as seeing the clear path and the unbeliever as blind.
rows.anchor: لما بين الهدى والضلالة ولم يهتد الكافر ، وهدى الله المؤمن من ضرب لهم مثلا بالبصير والأعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind and seeing represent believer and unbeliever; darkness and light represent unbelief and faith, with the unbeliever burdened by blindness as well as darkness.
rows.anchor: وقال الإيمان نور والمؤمن بصير والبصير لا يخفى عليه النور ، والكفر ظلمة والكافر أعمى فله صاد فوق صاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shade and scorching heat depict their outcomes: through faith the believer has shade and comfort, while through unbelief the disbeliever has heat and hardship.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر لمآلهما ومرجعهما مثلا وهو الظل والحرور ، فالمؤمن بإيمانه في ظل وراحة والكافر بكفره في حر وتعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The living and dead are another comparison: a blind person shares some perception with the seeing, but an unbeliever has no beneficial perception and is like the dead; the repeated verb sets this image apart.
rows.anchor: فإن الأعمى يشارك البصير في إدراك ما . والكافر غير مدرك إدراكا نافعا فهو كالميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negation repeats where the contrasts are strongest: darkness and light, and shade and heat, are direct opposites; life and death differ more essentially than seeing and blindness, so the final contrast also merits emphasis.
rows.anchor: التكرير للتأكيد والمنافاة بين الظلمة والنور والظل والحرور مضادة ، فالظلمة تنافي النور وتضاده والعمى والبصر كذلك
